summary: A string is text in quotes. Use length to count its characters, an index to get one character, and === to compare two strings.
notes: song.length counts every character, including spaces.
song[0] is the first character. song[song.length - 1] is the last.
=== compares the text, and the comparison is case-sensitive.
pitfall: Writing song.length() with parentheses, as in Java, causes TypeError: song.length is not a function.
contrast: JavaScript uses s.length with no parentheses, where Python uses len(s) and Java uses s.length(). === compares the text like Python's ==, so you do not need Java's equals().
